nodes.description:
The rate-limiting node, and the one that makes this disease mechanistically interesting. ARPC1B-null platelets contain no ARPC1B and greatly reduced Arp2/3 complex, while the other five components are present at normal levels. So the complex is not merely missing a part; without this particular subunit it does not assemble.
ARPC1A is the obvious candidate substitute - same slot, 68% identity - and it is actively upregulated in ARPC1B-deficient cells. It does not rescue. Some ARPC1A does appear in the residual Arp2/3 of null platelets, where none is detectable in normal platelets, so the substitution physically happens and is simply not sufficient. The authors' conclusion, that the ARPC1 isoforms are not functionally interchangeable, is the human genetic evidence for a proposition that had only been argued experimentally.

nodes.description:
Variants are diverse and scattered across the gene - frameshift, missense affecting the WD40 repeats, and splice-site - and in every patient tested the ARPC1B protein is undetectable on immunoblot. A splice-site founder variant, c.64+2T>A, accounts for a Nepalese cluster and is associated with a more severe course than other alleles.
The WD40 repeats matter structurally: six of them form the beta-propeller through which ARPC1B contacts the mother actin filament, so a truncation removing five of the six removes the interaction surface rather than merely shortening the protein.

nodes.description: Very early onset - a mean of two months, with a range of one to six - and a triad that would ordinarily suggest three diagnoses: susceptibility to infection, allergy, and autoimmune inflammation. Recurrent or severe respiratory infection in 71% and skin infection in 50%; eczema in 57% with food allergy and asthma; cutaneous vasculitis in 69%, leukocytoclastic on every biopsy performed; arthritis in 23%. IgA and IgE are markedly raised in almost all cases, while the antibody response to polysaccharide vaccine is normal - unlike Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome or DOCK8 deficiency.

nodes.description:
Arp2/3 nucleates a daughter filament off the side of an existing one, which is how cells build the branched networks that drive lamellipodia, phagocytosis, endocytosis, vesicular trafficking and immune-synapse formation. Losing it does not abolish actin polymerisation - patient platelets still spread, and still make prominent filopodia, which are unbranched bundles - it removes the branched arm specifically, leaving lamellipodia limited.
That morphological signature, filopodia preserved and lamellipodia lost, is the cellular fingerprint of the defect and is what connects the platelet, immune and DNA-repair arms below to one molecular lesion.

nodes.description:
The newest and least-explored arm. Arp2/3 has a nuclear role: it promotes chromatin dynamics and drives clustering of DNA double-strand breaks for homology-directed repair. ARPC1B-deficient patient cells are radiosensitive by three independent methods, with more chromatid-type aberrations, more gamma-H2AX foci and more cells arrested in G2/M after ionising radiation or bleomycin.
This arm is curated separately rather than folded into the immune one because it is mechanistically distinct - it is nuclear, not cytoskeletal-motility - and because its clinical consequences are unknown. It was proposed as a disease trait in 2022 and has not been shown to cause any of the disease's manifestations.

nodes.description:
The immune arm has been resolved to specific cell types. Regulatory T cells expanded from patients show decreased FOXP3, Helios, CD25 and CTLA-4 and defective suppressor activity against both CD4 and CD8 responders - a cell-intrinsic Treg defect, which is the most economical explanation for exaggerated Th2 responses, IgE reactivity and autoimmunity in one disease. NK cells show impaired degranulation against K562 targets, and, as in Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, IL-2 restores it, which places the defect in signalling-dependent cytoskeletal remodelling rather than in the killing machinery.
Conventional T cells are reduced in number with a skewed naive compartment, but their proliferative responses are largely normal - so this is not a proliferation defect.

Patient platelets additionally have dense granule deficiencies and the spreading abnormality above.

nodes.description:
Bleeding is the presenting problem in most patients and is disproportionately gastrointestinal - enterorrhagia rather than the mucocutaneous bleeding a platelet count alone would predict. Nearly four in five patients in the largest cohort had recurrent or severe bleeding.
Whether these platelets are small is disputed, and the dispute is not cosmetic: platelet size is the classical bedside discriminator against Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome. See the controversy discussion below.
